[[Image:Impatiens walleriana.JPG|thumb|''Impatiens walleriana'']]

'''''Impatiens walleriana''''' ([[synonym (taxonomy)|syn.]] ''Impatiens sultanii''), also known as '''busy Lizzie''' (British Isles), '''balsam''', '''sultana''', or simply '''impatiens''', is a [[species]] of the [[genus]] ''[[Impatiens]]'', [[native plant|native]] to eastern Africa from Kenya to Mozambique. The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''walleriana'' honours a British missionary, [[Horace Waller (activist)|Horace Waller]] (1833–1896).<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book |last=Harrison |first=Lorraine |title=RHS Latin for Gardeners |year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley |location=United Kingdom |isbn=978-1845337315 }}</ref>

==Description==
It is a flowering [[herbaceous]] [[perennial plant]] growing to {{convert|15|-|60|cm|0|abbr=on}} tall, with broad [[lanceolate]] [[leaf|leaves]] 3–12 cm long and 2–5 cm broad. Leaves are mostly [[Phyllotaxis|alternate]], although they may be [[Phyllotaxis|opposite]] near the top of the plant. The changeable, simple leaves are stalked 1.5 to 6 cm long. The leaf blade is [[Glossary of botanical terms#ovate|ovate]] to broadly elliptic, sometimes obovate, 2.5 to 13 inches long and 2 to 5.5 inches wide, green and sometimes spotted or pink or reddish on the underside. [[Leaflet (botany)|Leaflet]]s are missing.<ref>Eckehart J. Jäger, Friedrich Ebel, Peter Hanelt, Gerd K. Müller (ed.): Rothmaler excursion flora of Germany. Volume 5: Herbaceous ornamental and useful plants. Spektrum Akademischer Verlag, Berlin Heidelberg 2008, {{ISBN|978-3-8274-0918-8}}</ref>

The hermaphroditic, [[zygomorphic]] [[flower]]s are profusely borne, 2–5 cm diameter, with five petals and a 1 cm spur. The seedpod explodes when ripe in the same manner as other ''Impatiens'' species, an evolutionary adaptation for [[Biological dispersal|seed dispersal]]. The lower sepals are slightly boat-shaped and narrow suddenly in the 2.8 to 4.5 inches long, thread-like curved, but not curved back spur. The stems are semi-succulent, and all parts of the plant (leaves, stems, flowers, roots) are soft and easily damaged.<ref name=RHSAZ />

==Cultivation==
[[File:Starr 070906-8884 Impatiens walleriana.jpg|thumb|Double impatiens]]
Although perennial in frost-free growing conditions, it is usually treated as a [[Hardiness (plants)|half-hardy]] [[Annual plant|annual]] in [[temperateness|temperate]] regions (though pot-grown plants can be successfully overwintered indoors). It is one of the most popular of all bedding plants for parks and gardens worldwide, typically grown in containers but also in [[Bedding (horticulture)|bedding]] schemes. [[Plant propagation|Propagation]] is by seed or stem cuttings (which often root readily in water).<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref>

===Cultivars===
Numerous [[cultivar]]s in a range of colours from white to purple, are widely available commercially, either as seeds or young plants. They include the following:
{{div col|colwidth=15em}}
*Accent series<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Impatiens'' Accent series|url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=3137|archive-url=https://archive.today/20121224043647/http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=3137|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 24, 2012|access-date=23 June 2013}}</ref>
*'Blackberry Ice'
*'Confection'
*'Eclipse'
*'Elfin White'
*'Extra Dwarf'
*'Fiesta Ole' ([[Double-flowered|double]] variety)
*'Lipstick'
*'Red Star'
*Super Elfin series<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Impatiens walleriana'' Super Elfin Series|url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=1026|archive-url=https://archive.today/20121224032816/http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=1026|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 24, 2012|access-date=23 June 2013}}</ref>
*Tempo Series<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Impatiens walleriana'' Tempo Series|url=http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=4733|access-date=23 June 2013|archive-date=7 August 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130807062558/http://apps.rhs.org.uk/plantselector/plant?plantid=4733|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*'Wink and Blink'
{{div col end}}

Super Elfin series was bred by Claude Hope in Costa Rica. Hope developed this species from its native wild form into one of the most popular bedding plants in the world.<ref>{{cite book | author=Pink, A. | url=https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11892|title=Gardening for the Million| year=2004 | publisher=[[Project Gutenberg|Project Gutenberg Literary Archive Foundation]]}}</ref>
